As @NotToBeContrarian says but doesn't explain too well you could try a "live" version. This is a DVD image that you download and burn into a blank DVD or write into an USB pen-drive. Once you restart your computer with the DVD or USB inside the computer will turn on on Linux through it instead of Windows. The DVD/USB is not able to make changes to your hard drive so it's perfectly safe but it can read your files so you can see "live" how it would be to use your computer with Linux instead of Windows.

Of course there are some problems with this method: it's a lot slower than an installed Linux, it will reset itself every time you boot it again (since it cannot write to your hard-drive to "remember" anything next time), etc. It's pretty basic but good for you to try Linux out.

I would suggest you try a live version that comes with Gnome installed and another with KDE - unlike Windows you can actually choose what desktop technology you want to be using and these are the most widely used (easier to find help about on the web, etc). If after trying out you like what you see it should be easy for you to make a proper install alongside windows with KDE or GNOME.
